sections.name: File setup, slugOf, summary
sections.title: Setup and room naming helpers
sections.what: Brings in the event shape, sport list, replay data, story and chase model code, the rights lookup and the room types. Defines how a room's web name is made from its source and reference, and a short room summary.
sections.why: Likely reason: a stable, unique name keeps each room's link fixed.
sections.watch_out: Changing the source or reference format changes every room link.

sections.name: sportRooms
sections.title: Lists events for one sport
sections.what: Returns the rooms available for a sport, or the reason the sport has none yet, such as no recorded events.
sections.why: The purpose comment says sports without data must say so.
sections.watch_out: The pending reason is only used when a sport has no events at all.

sections.name: ballLabel
sections.title: Turns ball count into an over label
sections.what: Turns a count of legal balls bowled into a readable over and ball label, such as 17.3, meaning the ball about to be bowled.
sections.watch_out: Assumes six legal balls per over, which holds for cricket.

sections.name: eventRoom
sections.title: Builds one event's room
sections.what: Finds the event for a sport and slug, works out the observed range and proof, builds the chase win chart and peak leverage if a chase exists, otherwise a reason no model applies, adds stories with proof, and adds the credit line. Returns nothing if the event is not found.
sections.why: The header says numbers come from recorded incidents or the exact chase model.
sections.watch_out: Assumes 120 legal balls per innings, so a shortened match is charted on the wrong time scale, and the observed-range fields are undefined when there are no incidents.

sections.name: allRooms
sections.title: All room links for static pages
sections.what: Lists every room's sport and slug so the site can build a page for each.
sections.why: The comment says this is for static generation.
sections.watch_out: It reads the replay data at build time, so new events appear only after that data is refreshed.

summary: Builds the Event Room pages: a list of recorded events for each sport, and a detailed room for one event with its win chart, leverage peak, stories and credit line.
purpose: Presents recorded matches as rooms, showing only numbers that come from recorded data or the exact model. Sports without a model say so.
why: The header says every number comes from recorded incidents or the exact chase model.
how: 1. Lists events for a sport from the replay data, or gives the reason none exist. 2. Builds one event's room: finds it, works out the observed range and its proof, builds the chase win chart and peak leverage if a chase exists, otherwise gives a reason no model applies, attaches stories with their proof, and adds the credit line. 3. Lists all rooms for static pages.
inputs: A sport name and a room slug.
outputs: Room summaries, the reason a sport is pending, and full room data.
risks: The 120-ball limit is hard-coded for a 20-over innings, so other formats give wrong charts. The first observed time comes from the first element, so an event with no incidents gives undefined values. The proof label is fixed to delayed verified data on a replay clock.
debug: If a room is missing, check the sport and slug. If the chart looks shifted, check the 120-ball assumption. If a sport shows as pending, read the pending reason.
